2607.01018.title: Reading Order Inference for Complex Document Layouts
2607.01018.paper_summary: Reading order inference remains a critical bottleneck in the digitization of complex historical manuscripts, where pages contain multiple spatially interleaved reading streams, the canonical example being the Glossa Ordinaria layout, in which a central text is surrounded by commentaries that wrap around it in non-rectangular, non-convex regions. We present a training-free, graph-based framework: each OCR text line becomes a node in a directed candidate-transition graph, edges are scored by a weighted additive ensemble of two lightweight language-model signals (causal language model conditional likelihood and BERT next-sentence prediction, NSP; a third sentence-embedding signal was evaluated but did not improve reading order), and the global reading order is recovered as a degree-constrained directed path cover. To avoid the cascading "edge-theft" failures of greedy edge selection, we propose a max-regret inference rule that prioritizes commitments with high opportunity cost. We evaluate on synthetic Glossa Ordinaria grid layouts, on 23 ALTO page geometries (10 historical source pages plus mirrored and flipped variants), and on a 140-page multi-column English subset of OmniDocBench, comparing our method against the canonical recursive XY-cut (PaddleOCR PP-StructureV3) and two LayoutReader variants (layout-only and text+layout) on identical inputs. On wrap-around Glossa layouts our method recovers 95% of ground-truth successor edges on average vs. XY-cut's 50%; on the OmniDocBench multi-column subset it reaches 88% macro edge accuracy versus XY-cut's 75% and LayoutReader's 25%. The LayoutReader baselines transfer poorly due to a word-level vs. line-level granularity mismatch. We additionally verify mirror-invariance under horizontal and vertical page reflections: Our method changes by less than 1 percentage point, classical XY-cut by 2 points, and LayoutReader-T by up to 8 points.
2607.01018.paper_summary_zh: 閱讀順序推斷仍然是複雜歷史手稿數位化中的一個關鍵瓶頸，這些手稿的頁面包含多個空間交錯的閱讀流，典型的例子是 Glossa Ordinaria 的佈局，其中中央文本被環繞的註釋包圍，這些註釋在非矩形、非凸的區域內環繞著中央文本。我們提出了一個無需訓練的基於圖的框架：每一行 OCR 文本成為有向候選轉換圖中的一個節點，邊緣由兩個輕量級語言模型信號的加權加法集成進行評分（因果語言模型條件似然和 BERT 下一句預測，NSP；第三個句子嵌入信號被評估但未改善閱讀順序），全球閱讀順序則作為一個度約束的有向路徑覆蓋來恢復。為了避免貪婪邊緣選擇的級聯「邊緣盜竊」失敗，我們提出了一個最大後悔推斷規則，優先考慮具有高機會成本的承諾。我們在合成的 Glossa Ordinaria 網格佈局上進行評估，在 23 個 ALTO 頁面幾何圖形（10 個歷史來源頁面以及鏡像和翻轉變體）上進行評估，並在 OmniDocBench 的 140 頁多列英語子集上進行評估，將我們的方法與經典的遞歸 XY-cut（PaddleOCR PP-StructureV3）和兩個 LayoutReader 變體（僅佈局和文本+佈局）在相同的輸入上進行比較。在包裹式 Glossa 佈局中，我們的方法平均恢復了 95% 的真實後繼邊緣，而 XY-cut 則為 50%；在 OmniDocBench 的多列子集中，它達到了 88% 的宏邊緣準確率，而 XY-cut 為 75%，LayoutReader 為 25%。由於字級別與行級別的粒度不匹配，LayoutReader 基準的轉移效果較差。我們還驗證了在水平和垂直頁面反射下的鏡像不變性：我們的方法變化小於 1 個百分點，經典的 XY-cut 變化 2 個百分點，LayoutReader-T 變化最多達到 8 個百分點。
